stories.title_orig: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
stories.summary_orig: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40…
stories.title_vi: Sage-Med: Mở rộng trí tuệ đa phương thức trong lĩnh vực y tế
stories.summary_vi: Việc thiết lập các quy luật mở rộng quy mô hiệu quả cho các mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn đa phương thức y tế (MLLM) vẫn là một thách thức dai dẳng và cơ bản. Đánh giá có hệ thống của chúng tôi cho thấy các MLLM y tế hiện có có xu hướng hoạt động kém hơn các MLLM đa dụng tiên tiến trong nhiều nhiệm vụ y tế. Trong khi đó, việc mở rộng quy mô mô hình chủ yếu cải thiện khả năng xử lý văn bản hơn là khả năng nhận thức đa phương thức, và việc kích hoạt các chế độ suy luận không thể thu hẹp khoảng cách về khả năng xử lý hình ảnh này.

stories.title_orig: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
stories.summary_orig: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.
stories.title_vi: ROAM-Bench: Đánh giá trí tuệ không gian chủ động gắn liền với cơ thể thông qua xác minh bằng chứng
stories.summary_vi: Trí thông minh không gian gắn liền với cơ thể đòi hỏi agents phải thu thập thông tin thông qua việc khám phá và tương tác, sau đó sử dụng thông tin đó để suy luận và hành động. Các benchmarks hiện có không phân biệt đầy đủ giữa kết quả chính xác và việc hoàn thành các yêu cầu nhiệm vụ này. Chúng tôi giới thiệu ROAM-Bench để đánh giá các khả năng này trong điều kiện có các ràng buộc về chuyển động và va chạm của robot.

stories.title_orig: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding
stories.summary_orig: Multi-page document vision-language models encode each page independently, creating a feature-level discontinuity at page boundaries: visual tokens are formed without access to content on adjacent pages, and the language model must reason over these page representations formed in isolation. We introduce DocSEAM (Document Selective Enrichment via Anchored Masking), a lightweight module inserted between a pretrained vision encoder and the language model that injects the inductive bias of local cross-page context into visual representations. For each page, DocSEAM forms a local triplet with its two neighbors, applies center-anchored masked self-attention with directional salience gates to fuse information from neighbor pages, and returns only the enriched center-page tokens, leaving the visual token count unchanged. After a supervised cross-page warm-up and multi-page fine-tuning with DocSEAM frozen, our 9B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art results among the evaluated open-weight models of up to 10B parameters on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks. We further show that under controlled re-pagination, DocSEAM reduces sensitivity to boundary placement and improves…

stories.title_orig: Playfulness as Feedback for Agentic Game Development
stories.summary_orig: Coding agents can generate runnable games from natural-language descriptions. However, a runnable game does not guarantee an excellent gameplay experience for players. In our view, a playful game should provide 1) reliable core functionality, 2) appealing visual design and assets, and 3) rich gameplay that supports exploration and progression. How agents can improve these aspects of playfulness remains underexplored. In our work, we propose Play2Evolve, a recursive game development framework with three stages: Initialization, Refinement, and Evolution. Using playfulness as feedback, agents playtest the game and diagnose issues in its functionality, visual presentation, and gameplay. Their feedback guides bug fixes and asset improvements. It also helps agents propose new gameplay and aesthetic goals for continued game evolution. To enrich game materials, we combine a video generation model with code to create appealing static and dynamic assets and integrate them into interactive gameplay. Finally, Play2Evolve achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods, scoring 60.05 on GameCraft-Bench compared with 50.81 after Game Initialization and 52.46 for Play2Code…
stories.title_vi: Tính vui nhộn như một phản hồi cho việc phát triển trò chơi Agentic
stories.summary_vi: Lập trình agents có thể tạo ra các trò chơi có thể chạy được từ các mô tả bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên. Tuy nhiên, một trò chơi có thể chạy được không đảm bảo mang lại trải nghiệm chơi game tuyệt vời cho người chơi. Theo quan điểm của chúng tôi, một trò chơi thú vị cần có 1) chức năng cốt lõi đáng tin cậy, 2) thiết kế và tài nguyên hình ảnh hấp dẫn, và 3) lối chơi phong phú hỗ trợ việc khám phá và tiến triển. Vấn đề agents có thể cải thiện những khía cạnh này của tính thú vị như thế nào vẫn chưa được nghiên cứu kỹ lưỡng.

stories.title_orig: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
stories.summary_orig: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story. Agent systems provide such memory for offline multi-shot generation, yet they read the whole script in advance, plan each shot before generating it, and regenerate failed shots, which a live stream does not allow. We present Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous agentic memory for long video generation. A memory agent on separate GPUs reads only the prompts revealed so far, never the generated video, and keeps a text state and evolving images for every person, object, and scene. From this entity memory it composes a global image and a per-shot memory image, which an auxiliary GPU prefills into the generator's attention sink before the next shot starts, and writes entity cards for the prompts that name them, so the video never waits for memory and video errors are not written back. A small language model, trained with reinforcement learning and an image reward calibrated using downstream video outcomes, decides what to remember before the next prompt is known. stories.title_orig: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
stories.summary_orig: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Recent feed-forward pointmap methods eliminate the need for camera poses but inherently produce discrete, sparse representations. In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Our approach first extracts explicit geometric priors using a pre-trained pointmap model. A query-view-centric selection module then identifies geometrically relevant reference views via a robust surfel voting mechanism. Next, a cross-attention regressor bridges target query rays with reference features to estimate a continuous coarse surface. Lastly, a raylet-based module aggregates local 3D features to carve out high-frequency details and analytical normals. Trained as a single foundation model on 9 diverse datasets, our method demonstrates exceptional zero-shot generalization on 6 unseen datasets, clearly surpassing state-of-the-art baselines in geometric accuracy and detail preservation.
stories.title_vi: FoundSurface: Tái tạo bề mặt cảnh 3D dựa trên tia phản hồi từ các hình ảnh không được sắp xếp

stories.title_orig: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
stories.summary_orig: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to N times M integrations when evaluating N methods on M benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our…

Tuy nhiên, mỗi benchmark riêng lẻ đều xác định các đầu vào, sản phẩm bàn giao và quy trình chấm điểm của riêng mình.

stories.title_orig: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
stories.summary_orig: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents inspect their drafts throughout production. Multimodal perception runs in short-lived contexts kept apart from the coder and returns compact, grounded Findings. Seven primitives operate on a unified multi-clock representation of assets and drafts: they explore media from coarse to fine, verify quoted requirements with evidence from every required modality, compare a draft with a reference or an earlier revision on separate clocks, and measure stream signals locally…

stories.title_orig: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
stories.summary_orig: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user…

stories.title_orig: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
stories.summary_orig: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current…

stories.title_orig: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
stories.summary_orig: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. Meanwhile, existing image- and video-based methods may generate unseen regions but produce inconsistent geometry across views. To bridge this gap, we present WorldBridge, a framework for coherent and controllable 3D world generation under scattered images with little or no visual overlap. WorldBridge encodes scattered references into a global scene context to guide geometry and appearance generation across views. Our temporal and spatial reference attention mechanism further enhances the fidelity of temporal references along the target trajectory and supports flexible spatial references outside it. A plug-and-play latent-reference consistency strategy improves reference fidelity through reprojection-guided test-time optimization. We also introduce the WorldBridge benchmark suite to evaluate 3D world generation from scattered, low-overlap references, which is rarely explored by current benchmarks. Both qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method…
stories.title_vi: WorldBridge: Kết nối các góc nhìn rời rạc để tạo ra thế giới 3D nhất quán
stories.summary_vi: Việc tạo ra các thế giới 3D mạch lạc và có thể khám phá từ các hình ảnh rời rạc, ít hoặc không có sự chồng chéo về mặt hình ảnh, là một thách thức cơ bản và lâu dài trong lĩnh vực thị giác máy tính, mà các phương pháp hiện có có tính đến yếu tố hình học không thể giải quyết được. Trong khi đó, các phương pháp dựa trên hình ảnh và video hiện có có thể tạo ra các vùng chưa từng thấy nhưng lại tạo ra hình học không nhất quán giữa các góc nhìn.

stories.title_orig: RoboEvo^2: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
stories.summary_orig: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo^2, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy provides stronger motor skills for subsequent search, while its remaining failures redirect harness evolution, closing the reciprocal loop. Through…
stories.title_vi: RoboEvo^2: Robot tự cải thiện đệ quy thông qua sự đồng tiến hóa giữa bộ dây và chính sách
stories.summary_vi: Robot cần thích nghi với các môi trường không quen thuộc và tiếp thu các kỹ năng mới thông qua tương tác, sau đó thực hiện các kỹ năng đó một cách hiệu quả nhờ luyện tập. stories.title_orig: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
stories.summary_orig: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. stories.title_vi: PyRUA-Dex: Học các chính sách lập trình để thao tác khéo léo bằng hai tay với mã hóa Agents
stories.summary_vi: Việc học để thao tác khéo léo bị hạn chế do thiếu các minh họa chất lượng cao: việc điều chỉnh mục tiêu từ video của con người là không chính xác, điều khiển từ xa không cung cấp phản hồi lực cho người vận hành và việc thu thập dữ liệu dựa trên bộ xương ngoài rất khó mở rộng quy mô. Chúng tôi xin giới thiệu PyRUA-Dex, một khung kiến trúc cho phép mã hóa agents để phát triển thao tác khéo léo thông qua chính sách lập trình, mà không cần các lượt minh họa.

stories.title_orig: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
stories.summary_orig: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework for improving LLMs at test time through two mutually reinforcing components: (1) In-Context RSI repeatedly re-solves each question using the full previous solution as a reference, letting the model decide whether and how to use it so that inference compute builds on earlier reasoning. (2) In-Weight RSI distills successive refinements into the model's weights, enabling progress beyond an initially wrong majority and theoretically bringing the first attempt toward the…
stories.title_vi: Vượt ra ngoài tính nhất quán tự thân: Tự cải thiện đệ quy tại thời điểm kiểm tra
stories.summary_vi: Các mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn (LLMs) tiếp tục được cải thiện sau khi triển khai (ví dụ: tự cải thiện đệ quy) mở ra một con đường đầy hứa hẹn hướng tới trí tuệ tổng quát. Các phương pháp thời gian kiểm thử hiện tại theo đuổi mục tiêu này đối với các câu hỏi chưa được gắn nhãn, chủ yếu dựa trên tính nhất quán nội tại: chúng tạo ra các giải pháp độc lập và sử dụng phương thức bỏ phiếu theo đa số để chọn câu trả lời hoặc xây dựng các mục tiêu đào tạo.

stories.title_orig: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
stories.summary_orig: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object…
stories.title_vi: Vượt ra ngoài Con đường hạnh phúc: Tổng quát hóa các mô hình thế giới robot từ các lỗi mô phỏng

stories.title_orig: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
stories.summary_orig: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. We evaluate four controlled observation corruptions through a visual-corruption extension of RoboTwin, termed RoboTwin-Plus; HOG-WAM achieves the highest success among the compared policies under all four. Mixed-noise success increases from 78.86% to 82.86% relative to FastWAM, with comparable performance on clean scenes. On LIBERO Plus, overall success increases from 74.49% to 75.26%, with the largest gain under sensor noise, from 74.14% to 78.89%. Across four Franka tasks, average success increases from 40% to 59% under clean observations and from 17% to 24% under noisy observations. A representation ablation favors…
stories.title_vi: HOG-WAM: Cải thiện độ ổn định hình ảnh thông qua dự đoán gradient tương lai
stories.summary_vi: Các mô hình hành động trong thế giới cùng nhau dự đoán các quan sát và hành động trong tương lai, tuy nhiên, sự suy giảm chất lượng hình ảnh có thể làm gián đoạn các chính sách thu được. Chúng tôi giới thiệu HOG-WAM, mô hình bổ sung các Biểu đồ tần suất của các Gradient theo hướng (HOG) trong tương lai dưới dạng giám sát cấu trúc được rút ra trực tiếp từ các hình ảnh minh họa.

stories.title_orig: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
stories.summary_orig: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly process the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens, enabling direct pixel-space prediction without additional condition encoders or adapters. With pixel-accurate synthetic supervision and real-image fine-tuning, PixelMatte predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass. Two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner, further improve regional opacity accuracy and boundary fidelity. Experiments across four benchmarks and two distinct pixel…
stories.title_vi: Tách nền ảnh độ nét cao bằng phương pháp khuếch tán trong không gian pixel Transformers
stories.summary_vi: Các mô hình khuếch tán đã cho thấy tiềm năng mạnh mẽ trong việc tách nền hình ảnh bằng cách chuyển giao các thông tin tiên nghiệm sinh thành được học từ quá trình tiền đào tạo quy mô lớn. Tuy nhiên, các phương pháp hiện có phần lớn dựa vào các mô hình khuếch tán tiềm ẩn, trong đó các biểu diễn nén và tái tạo dựa trên VAE gây ra sự không khớp với độ chính xác tần số cao cần thiết cho việc tách nền.

stories.title_orig: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
stories.summary_orig: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query, models receive only the observation prefix available at that time; decision-aware metrics reward calibrated waiting and complete reactions while penalizing premature commitment. Evaluating 45 proprietary and open-source general-purpose, embodied, streaming-video, and omni-modal models reveals fragmented and temporally miscalibrated competence. General-purpose VLMs excel at passive cue grounding and intent recognition, whereas embodied specialists lead on isolated reaction sub-decisions; yet across…
stories.title_vi: AIRIS: Đánh giá so sánh trí tuệ xã hội gắn liền với cơ thể trong các video phát trực tuyến theo góc nhìn người thứ nhất

stories.title_orig: iMFPO: Improving Mean Flow Policy Optimization with Drift-Aware Velocity Alignment for Embodied Control
stories.summary_orig: Flow-based generative policies offer expressive action modeling for embodied control, yet achieving efficient one-step generation under reward-driven policy optimization remains challenging. In particular, evolving action distributions during online reinforcement learning may introduce inconsistencies between instantaneous-velocity learning and interval-averaged action generation. To address this challenge, we propose iMFPO, a one-step generative policy optimization framework with decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment. A shared interval-conditioned actor supports instantaneous-velocity supervision and interval-averaged action generation. JVP-corrected velocity regression is jointly optimized with reward-driven policy objectives, with action-level guidance from a frozen PPO teacher during training. At inference, iMFPO directly generates actions through interval-averaged velocity prediction, achieving one-step control without iterative flow integration. Across Go2, G1, H1, and Spot, zero-latent evaluation yields mean returns of 35.69, 34.44, 416.23, and 29.86. On Go2, action-generation latency drops from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms relative to 64-step RFPO. stories.title_vi: iMFPO: Cải thiện tối ưu hóa chính sách dòng chảy trung bình với sự liên kết vận tốc có tính đến sự trôi dạt cho điều khiển gắn liền
stories.summary_vi: Các chính sách tạo sinh dựa trên luồng cung cấp mô hình hóa hành động biểu cảm cho việc điều khiển hiện thực hóa, tuy nhiên, việc đạt được khả năng tạo sinh một bước hiệu quả trong điều kiện tối ưu hóa chính sách theo phần thưởng vẫn còn là một thách thức. Đặc biệt, sự thay đổi của các phân phối hành động trong quá trình học tăng cường trực tuyến có thể gây ra sự không nhất quán giữa việc học vận tốc tức thời và việc tạo ra hành động trung bình theo khoảng thời gian.

stories.title_orig: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
stories.summary_orig: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.
stories.title_vi: Vượt ra ngoài mã lệnh và điểm ảnh: Cùng tạo ra các bài thuyết trình có thể chỉnh sửa và phong phú về mặt hình ảnh
stories.summary_vi: Tạo các bản thuyết trình PPTX là một nhiệm vụ có cấu trúc đòi hỏi phải có sự lập kế hoạch ngữ nghĩa, bố cục trực quan, sắp xếp chính xác và khả năng chỉnh sửa, từ đó thúc đẩy sự hợp tác giữa các agents chuyên môn. Tuy nhiên, các phương pháp lập trình cho phép chỉnh sửa nhưng thường tạo ra các thiết kế cứng nhắc, trong khi các phương pháp dựa trên hình ảnh mang lại sự phong phú về mặt hình ảnh nhưng lại làm phẳng nội dung thành các điểm ảnh khó chỉnh sửa.

stories.title_orig: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
stories.summary_orig: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, model-driven context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~rightarrow~56\%), and Kimi gains with up to 41\% fewer input tokens. Models differ widely, however, in how often they use the API, how aggressively they compact, and when they start compacting, and prompt changes shift that timing. Finally, we show that inference engines can make model-driven edits cheaper: by reusing the KV cache of the unchanged suffix after an edit, we cut prefill compute by up to 15\% per request with no measurable change in accuracy. stories.summary_orig: A new version of the SYS01 infostealer malware delivered through Meta ads is enrolling browsers into enterprise-style management to force the installation of an extension that steals sensitive data, including Gmail and Outlook emails.
stories.title_vi: SYS010 malware lợi dụng tính năng quản lý trình duyệt để theo dõi Gmail, Outlook
stories.summary_vi: Một phiên bản mới của phần mềm đánh cắp thông tin SYS01 malware được phát tán thông qua các quảng cáo Meta đang ghi danh các trình duyệt vào chế độ quản lý kiểu doanh nghiệp để buộc cài đặt một tiện ích mở rộng có khả năng đánh cắp dữ liệu nhạy cảm, bao gồm cả email Gmail và Outlook.

stories.title_orig: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
stories.summary_orig: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework. For context management, we find that preserving individually accessible records of past attempts is more effective than maintaining a rolling summary, with context folding performing best across all six settings and improving upon the baseline by up to 19.2%. stories.title_vi: Làm sáng tỏ bộ công cụ nghiên cứu tự động: Bối cảnh và kỹ năng định hình sự tự phát triển như thế nào Agents
stories.summary_vi: Các hệ thống nghiên cứu tự động agents, có khả năng tự động thiết kế, chạy và tinh chỉnh các thí nghiệm, đang đẩy nhanh tiến bộ khoa học, đặc biệt là trong nghiên cứu AI. Tuy nhiên, các agents hiện có dựa vào các bộ dây nối kết hợp nhiều cơ chế, khiến việc xác định mức độ đóng góp của từng thành phần riêng lẻ vào hiệu suất trở nên khó khăn.
